<p>While the usual <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="O(n \log{n})" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="O"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D442">𝑂</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mo data-latex="("><mjx-c class="mjx-c28">(</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mi data-latex="n"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D45B">𝑛</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mi space="2" data-latex="\log"><mjx-c class="mjx-c6C" noic="true" style="padding-top: 0.694em;">l</mjx-c><mjx-c class="mjx-c6F" noic="true" style="padding-top: 0.694em;">o</mjx-c><mjx-c class="mjx-c67" style="padding-top: 0.694em;">g</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mo><mjx-c class="mjx-c2061">⁡</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-TeXAtom space="2" data-latex="{n}" texclass="ORD"><mjx-mi data-latex="n"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D45B">𝑛</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-TeXAtom><mjx-mo data-latex=")"><mjx-c class="mjx-c29">)</mjx-c></mjx-mo></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="O(n \log{n})"><mi data-latex="O">O</mi><mo data-latex="(" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi data-latex="n">n</mi><mi data-latex="\log">log</mi><mo data-mjx-texclass="NONE">⁡</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD" data-latex="{n}"><mi data-latex="n">n</mi></mrow><mo data-latex=")" stretchy="false">)</mo></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> suffix array algorithm described <a href="https://cp-algorithms.com/string/suffix-array.html">here</a> suffices for almost all of one's competitive-programming needs, suffix structures turn out to be useful in several other fields which require faster algorithms. Lossless compression is one such field, and I happened to need a faster SA algorithm in an LZ-compressor I've <a href="https://github.com/welcome-to-the-sunny-side/misa77">been working on recently</a>.</p>
<p>In this blog, we'll learn how to build suffix arrays in linear time, using the algorithm I learned for this purpose. It's called SA-IS ("Suffix Array by Induced Sorting", by Nong, Zhang, and Chan), and was originally described <a href="https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/4976463">in this paper</a>.</p>

<p>Now, theorem 2.4 is quite powerful as it allows us to characterise the structure of the suffix array in a very friendly "bucketed" manner. We can observe that the suffix array must take the following form:</p>
<ul>
<li>First, we have L-type suffixes that start with symbol <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="0" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mn data-latex="0"><mjx-c class="mjx-c30">0</mjx-c></mjx-mn></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="0"><mn data-latex="0">0</mn></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>.</li>
<li>Then, we have S-type suffixes that start with symbol <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="0" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mn data-latex="0"><mjx-c class="mjx-c30">0</mjx-c></mjx-mn></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="0"><mn data-latex="0">0</mn></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>.</li>
<li>Then, L-type suffixes that start with symbol <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="1" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mn data-latex="1"><mjx-c class="mjx-c31">1</mjx-c></mjx-mn></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="1"><mn data-latex="1">1</mn></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>.</li>
<li>Then, S-type suffixes that start with symbol <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="1" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mn data-latex="1"><mjx-c class="mjx-c31">1</mjx-c></mjx-mn></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="1"><mn data-latex="1">1</mn></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>.</li>
<li>Then, L-type suffixes that start with symbol <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="2" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mn data-latex="2"><mjx-c class="mjx-c32">2</mjx-c></mjx-mn></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="2"><mn data-latex="2">2</mn></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>.</li>
<li>Then, S-type suffixes that start with symbol <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="2" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mn data-latex="2"><mjx-c class="mjx-c32">2</mjx-c></mjx-mn></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="2"><mn data-latex="2">2</mn></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>.</li>
<li>...and so on</li>
</ul>
<p>In other words:</p>
<ul>
<li>The suffix array consists of several disjoint buckets, with each bucket corresponding to suffixes starting with a certain symbol.</li>
<li>The buckets are ordered by the starting symbol.</li>
<li>Within a particular bucket, we first have all the L-type suffixes, and then all the S-type suffixes.</li>
</ul>
<p>It's easy to see that these bucket boundaries can also be computed in <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="O(n)" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="O"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D442">𝑂</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mo data-latex="("><mjx-c class="mjx-c28">(</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mi data-latex="n"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D45B">𝑛</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mo data-latex=")"><mjx-c class="mjx-c29">)</mjx-c></mjx-mo></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="O(n)"><mi data-latex="O">O</mi><mo data-latex="(" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi data-latex="n">n</mi><mo data-latex=")" stretchy="false">)</mo></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>. It might seem odd that I'm mentioning this, but it's important for the implementation later.</p>
<details><summary class="spoiler-summary">Code</summary>
<div class="spoiler-content">
<pre class="hljs"><code><span class="hljs-comment">// Given n and T</span>
<span class="hljs-type">int</span> n;
vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> T;

<span class="hljs-function">vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> <span class="hljs-title">cnt</span><span class="hljs-params">(n + <span class="hljs-number">1</span>, <span class="hljs-number">0</span>)</span></span>;
<span class="hljs-keyword">for</span>(<span class="hljs-keyword">auto</span> x : T)
    cnt[x]++;

<span class="hljs-keyword">auto</span> tail = cnt;
<span class="hljs-keyword">for</span>(<span class="hljs-type">int</span> i = <span class="hljs-number">1</span>; i <= n; i++)
    tail[i] += tail[i - <span class="hljs-number">1</span>];

<span class="hljs-keyword">auto</span> head = tail;
<span class="hljs-keyword">for</span>(<span class="hljs-type">int</span> i = <span class="hljs-number">0</span>; i <= n; i ++)
    head[i] -= cnt[i];

<span class="hljs-comment">//now, bucket for element i is [head[i], tail[i])</span>

<h1>3. LMS-types</h1>
<p>We define a suffix <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="i" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="i"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D456">𝑖</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="i"><mi data-latex="i">i</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> to be of <strong>LMS-type</strong> (i.e. "Leftmost-S-type") iff:</p>
<ul>
<li><mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="i > 0" breakable="true" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="i"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D456">𝑖</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-break size="4"> </mjx-break><mjx-mo data-latex=">"><mjx-c class="mjx-c3E">></mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mn space="4" data-latex="0"><mjx-c class="mjx-c30">0</mjx-c></mjx-mn></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="i > 0"><mi data-latex="i">i</mi><mo data-latex=">">></mo><mn data-latex="0">0</mn></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container></li>
<li>Suffix <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="i" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="i"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D456">𝑖</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="i"><mi data-latex="i">i</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> is of S-type.</li>
<li>Suffix <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="i - 1" breakable="true" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="i"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D456">𝑖</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-break size="3"> </mjx-break><mjx-mo data-latex="-"><mjx-c class="mjx-c2212">−</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mn space="3" data-latex="1"><mjx-c class="mjx-c31">1</mjx-c></mjx-mn></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="i - 1"><mi data-latex="i">i</mi><mo data-latex="-">−</mo><mn data-latex="1">1</mn></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> is of L-type.</li>
</ul>
<p>Let <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="l_0 < l_1 < \dots < l_{m - 1}" breakable="true" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-msub data-latex="l_0"><mjx-mi data-latex="l"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D459">𝑙</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-script style="vertical-align: -0.15em;"><mjx-mn size="s" data-latex="0"><mjx-c class="mjx-c30">0</mjx-c></mjx-mn></mjx-script></mjx-msub><mjx-break size="4"> </mjx-break><mjx-mo data-latex="<"><mjx-c class="mjx-c3C"><</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-msub space="4" data-latex="l_1"><mjx-mi data-latex="l"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D459">𝑙</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-script style="vertical-align: -0.15em;"><mjx-mn size="s" data-latex="1"><mjx-c class="mjx-c31">1</mjx-c></mjx-mn></mjx-script></mjx-msub><mjx-break size="4"> </mjx-break><mjx-mo data-latex="<"><mjx-c class="mjx-c3C"><</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mo space="4"><mjx-c class="mjx-c22EF">⋯</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-break size="4"> </mjx-break><mjx-mo data-latex="<"><mjx-c class="mjx-c3C"><</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-msub space="4" data-latex="l_{m-1}"><mjx-mi data-latex="l"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D459">𝑙</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-script style="vertical-align: -0.15em;"><mjx-TeXAtom size="s" data-latex="{m-1}" texclass="ORD"><mjx-mi data-latex="m"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D45A">𝑚</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mo data-latex="-"><mjx-c class="mjx-c2212">−</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mn data-latex="1"><mjx-c class="mjx-c31">1</mjx-c></mjx-mn></mjx-TeXAtom></mjx-script></mjx-msub></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="l_0 < l_1 < \dots < l_{m - 1}"><msub data-latex="l_0"><mi data-latex="l">l</mi><mn data-latex="0">0</mn></msub><mo data-latex="<"><</mo><msub data-latex="l_1"><mi data-latex="l">l</mi><mn data-latex="1">1</mn></msub><mo data-latex="<"><</mo><mo>⋯</mo><mo data-latex="<"><</mo><msub data-latex="l_{m-1}"><mi data-latex="l">l</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD" data-latex="{m-1}"><mi data-latex="m">m</mi><mo data-latex="-">−</mo><mn data-latex="1">1</mn></mrow></msub></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> be the LMS positions of <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="T" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="T"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D447">𝑇</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="T"><mi data-latex="T">T</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>.</p>
<p>A key observation is that there are <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="m \leq \frac{n + 1}{2} " breakable="true" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="m"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D45A">𝑚</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-break size="4"> </mjx-break><mjx-mo data-latex="\leq"><mjx-c class="mjx-c2264">≤</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mfrac space="4" data-latex="\frac{n + 1}{2}"><mjx-frac><mjx-num><mjx-nstrut></mjx-nstrut><mjx-mrow size="s" data-latex="n + 1"><mjx-mi data-latex="n"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D45B">𝑛</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mo data-latex="+"><mjx-c class="mjx-c2B">+</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mn data-latex="1"><mjx-c class="mjx-c31">1</mjx-c></mjx-mn></mjx-mrow></mjx-num><mjx-dbox><mjx-dtable><mjx-line></mjx-line><mjx-row><mjx-den><mjx-dstrut></mjx-dstrut><mjx-mn size="s" data-latex="2"><mjx-c class="mjx-c32">2</mjx-c></mjx-mn></mjx-den></mjx-row></mjx-dtable></mjx-dbox></mjx-frac></mjx-mfrac></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="m \leq \frac{n + 1}{2} "><mi data-latex="m">m</mi><mo data-latex="\leq">≤</mo><mfrac data-latex="\frac{n + 1}{2}"><mrow data-latex="n + 1"><mi data-latex="n">n</mi><mo data-latex="+">+</mo><mn data-latex="1">1</mn></mrow><mn data-latex="2">2</mn></mfrac></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> LMS positions (the existence of each LMS position "consumes" a unique L-type and S-type). As you will later see, the efficiency of SAIS is dependent on this.</p>

<p>Now, let's introduce a very helpful visualisation for strings that I'll just call a "slope view". The slope view of any given string will be obtained by us drawing downward or upward slants between two adjacent suffixes based on the result of their comparison (i.e. the type of the left suffix).</p>
<p>Let's look at some visualisations for <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="T = " breakable="true" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="T"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D447">𝑇</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-break size="4"> </mjx-break><mjx-mo data-latex="="><mjx-c class="mjx-c3D">=</mjx-c></mjx-mo></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="T = "><mi data-latex="T">T</mi><mo data-latex="=">=</mo></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> <code>baacbcbacbccdaa$</code> (where <code>$</code> is the appended unique minimum). I know I said that <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="T" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="T"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D447">𝑇</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="T"><mi data-latex="T">T</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> will have integer elements, but an english alphabet string is just nicer to look at, and is no different computationally (just assign some integer to every letter).</p>

<p>A few observations:</p>
<ul>
<li>LMS-types correspond to <em>valleys</em> in the slope view.</li>
<li>An upward slope (from left to right) corresponds to S-type suffixes.</li>
<li>A downward slope corresponds to L-type suffixes.</li>
<li>The second-last character is always L-type, as the last character is the unique minimum. Since the last position is definitionally S-type, this also implies that it's always LMS-type.</li>
</ul>
<p>Also recall theorem 2.4. <h1>4. Induced sorting</h1>
<p>Now, after having tunnel-visioned on the classification of these L/S types for so long, let's return to our original goal of finding <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="A" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="A"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D434">𝐴</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="A"><mi data-latex="A">A</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>. Why did we do all of this? As it turns out, it's really convenient to sort L-suffixes and S-suffixes separately.</p>
<h2>4.1 L-induce</h2>
<p>Say we were tasked with producing <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="A" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="A"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D434">𝐴</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="A"><mi data-latex="A">A</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> partially, i.e. only at positions <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="i" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="i"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D456">𝑖</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="i"><mi data-latex="i">i</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> such that <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="A_i" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-msub data-latex="A_i"><mjx-mi data-latex="A"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D434">𝐴</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-script style="vertical-align: -0.15em;"><mjx-mi size="s" data-latex="i"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D456">𝑖</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-script></mjx-msub></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="A_i"><msub data-latex="A_i"><mi data-latex="A">A</mi><mi data-latex="i">i</mi></msub></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> was an L-type position. Does the problem get meaningfully easier?</p>
<p>The observation that the entire algorithm is built upon is that <em>we don't need any S-type suffixes except the LMS-types to induce the sorted order of L-type suffixes</em>.</p>

<p>The rest of subsection 4.1 will be spent realising an algorithm which does this.</p>
<p>Let's first consider a really inefficient procedure to sort L-type suffixes while only making use of LMS-types (besides the L-types). This is really the sort of algorithm where it's simpler to use an unambiguous, real programming language rather than pseudocode, so you'll have to bear with C++ snippets throughout.</p>

<li>First, we delete all indices in the L-bucket of <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="0" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mn data-latex="0"><mjx-c class="mjx-c30">0</mjx-c></mjx-mn></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="0"><mn data-latex="0">0</mn></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> (L-suffixes that begin with <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="0" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mn data-latex="0"><mjx-c class="mjx-c30">0</mjx-c></mjx-mn></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="0"><mn data-latex="0">0</mn></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>).</li>
<li>Then, LMS indices in the S-bucket of <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="0" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mn data-latex="0"><mjx-c class="mjx-c30">0</mjx-c></mjx-mn></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="0"><mn data-latex="0">0</mn></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>.</li>
<li>Then, all indices in the L-bucket of <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="1" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mn data-latex="1"><mjx-c class="mjx-c31">1</mjx-c></mjx-mn></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="1"><mn data-latex="1">1</mn></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>.</li>
<li>Then, LMS indices in the S-bucket of <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="1" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mn data-latex="1"><mjx-c class="mjx-c31">1</mjx-c></mjx-mn></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="1"><mn data-latex="1">1</mn></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container></li>

<p>The issue here is that while we don't need the heap <em>at all</em> to handle the L-regions, it's doing critical work for us in the S-regions.</p>
<p>In particular, we can already modify procedure 2 to run in linear time <em>for the L-regions</em> in the following manner:</p>
<details><summary class="spoiler-summary">Procedure 2.5</summary>
<div class="spoiler-content">
<pre class="hljs"><code>A = [-1] * (n + 1)

put {S[i], i} for all LMS-type i into heap H

<span class="pseudo-comment"># we iterate over the first character of suffixes</span>
for character c from 0 to n:

    <span class="pseudo-comment"># we first process the L-region of c</span>
    let A[l, r] be the L-region for c
    for i from l to r:
        extend2(A[i])
  
    <span class="pseudo-comment"># we then process the LMS-types of c, naively</span>
    while H is not empty and the smallest suffix in H begins with c:
        pop out {S[i], i}, the smallest element of H
        extend2(i)
</code></pre>
</div>
</details>
<p>Why is this correct? <p>Looking at the second stage for each <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="c" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="c"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D450">𝑐</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="c"><mi data-latex="c">c</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>, it's easy to see that the heap was only really responsible for sorting the LMS-suffixes (all insertions are before all deletions now, so we don't need its "online" nature, we just need the sorted order of all LMS suffixes). This brings us back to theorem 4.1. We don't really need the entirety of a pre-built <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="A'" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-msup data-latex="A'"><mjx-mi data-latex="A"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D434">𝐴</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-script style="vertical-align: 0.363em;"><mjx-mo size="s" data-latex="'"><mjx-c class="mjx-c2032 NCM-V">′</mjx-c></mjx-mo></mjx-script></mjx-msup></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="A'"><msup data-latex="A'"><mi data-latex="A">A</mi><mo data-mjx-alternate="1" data-latex="'">′</mo></msup></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> - we only need <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="G" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="G"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D43A">𝐺</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="G"><mi data-latex="G">G</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>!</p>
<p>Let's finally look at the L-induce procedure, which takes <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="G" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="G"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D43A">𝐺</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="G"><mi data-latex="G">G</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> and computes the L-regions of <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="A" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="A"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D434">𝐴</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="A"><mi data-latex="A">A</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>. An implementation choice here is that since the S-regions of <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="A" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="A"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D434">𝐴</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="A"><mi data-latex="A">A</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> are otherwise unused during this phase, we just put all LMS positions from the given <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="G" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="G"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D43A">𝐺</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="G"><mi data-latex="G">G</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> at the ends of their respective S-buckets in <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="A" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="A"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D434">𝐴</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="A"><mi data-latex="A">A</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>, preserving their order.</p>
<details><summary class="spoiler-summary">Procedure 3</summary>
<div class="spoiler-content">
<pre class="hljs"><code><span class="hljs-comment">// Given n, T, Q, and the bucket boundaries (see code in theorem 2.4)</span>
<span class="hljs-type">int</span> n;
vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> T, Q, head, tail;

<span class="hljs-comment">// Of course, given G too!</span>
vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> G;

<span class="hljs-function">vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> <span class="hljs-title">A</span><span class="hljs-params">(n + <span class="hljs-number">1</span>, <span class="hljs-number">-1</span>)</span></span>;       <span class="hljs-comment">//suffix array</span>

<span class="hljs-comment">// Seeding - we put LMS positions at the tails of their S-buckets </span>
<span class="hljs-built_in">reverse</span>(G.<span class="hljs-built_in">begin</span>(), G.<span class="hljs-built_in">end</span>());
<span class="hljs-keyword">for</span>(<span class="hljs-keyword">auto</span> i : G)
    A[--tail[T[i]]] = i;

<span class="hljs-keyword">auto</span> extend2 = [&](<span class="hljs-type">int</span> i) -> <span class="hljs-type">void</span>
{
    <span class="hljs-type">int</span> j = i - <span class="hljs-number">1</span>;
    <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span>(j >= <span class="hljs-number">0</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">and</span> <span class="hljs-built_in">is_L_type</span>(Q[j]))

};

<span class="hljs-comment">// induce L positions into A</span>
<span class="hljs-keyword">auto</span> l_induce = [&]() -> <span class="hljs-type">void</span>
{
    <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span>(<span class="hljs-type">int</span> i = <span class="hljs-number">0</span>; i <= n; i ++)
        <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span>(A[i] != <span class="hljs-number">-1</span>)
            <span class="hljs-built_in">extend2</span>(A[i]);
};
<span class="hljs-built_in">l_induce</span>();

<span class="hljs-comment">// clean up LMS types from A</span>
<span class="hljs-keyword">for</span>(<span class="hljs-type">int</span> i = <span class="hljs-number">0</span>; i <= n; i ++)
    <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span>(A[i] != <span class="hljs-number">-1</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">and</span> <span class="hljs-built_in">is_LMS_type</span>(Q[A[i]]))
        A[i] = <span class="hljs-number">-1</span>;
</code></pre>

<p>It's easy to see that this procedure is correct (it's just the previous procedure with the second stage for each <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="c" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="c"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D450">𝑐</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="c"><mi data-latex="c">c</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> made efficient), and that apart from the magical acquisition of <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="G" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="G"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D43A">𝐺</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="G"><mi data-latex="G">G</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>, it runs in <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="O(n)" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="O"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D442">𝑂</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mo data-latex="("><mjx-c class="mjx-c28">(</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mi data-latex="n"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D45B">𝑛</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mo data-latex=")"><mjx-c class="mjx-c29">)</mjx-c></mjx-mo></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="O(n)"><mi data-latex="O">O</mi><mo data-latex="(" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi data-latex="n">n</mi><mo data-latex=")" stretchy="false">)</mo></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> (placing LMS-positions into <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="A" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="A"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D434">𝐴</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="A"><mi data-latex="A">A</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>, L-induce itself, cleanup).</p>
<h2>4.2 S-induce</h2>
<p>Let us now deal with the S regions.</p>
<p>The basic idea is symmetrical - just like we processed L-suffixes in non-decreasing order to fill the L-regions (left to right in <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="A" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="A"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D434">𝐴</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="A"><mi data-latex="A">A</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>), we will process S-suffixes in <em>non-increasing</em> order to fill the S-regions (right to left). In the slope view, we previously inched upwards on slopes that were slanted upward from right to left, after having seeded the valleys (<mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="G" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="G"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D43A">𝐺</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="G"><mi data-latex="G">G</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>). Now, we will inch downwards on slopes that are slanted downward from right to left (remember the slant of slopes for S-suffixes). We have an advantage here though! The analogous seeds are going to be the "leftmost L" (LML) positions (peaks in the slope view), which lie in the L-regions of <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="A" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="A"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D434">𝐴</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="A"><mi data-latex="A">A</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>. Since we have already computed the L-regions, we already have the analogue of <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="G" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="G"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D43A">𝐺</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="G"><mi data-latex="G">G</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> here!</p>
<p>Anyway, let's look at the procedure and then talk about it:</p>
<details><summary class="spoiler-summary">Procedure 4</summary>
<div class="spoiler-content">
<pre class="hljs"><code><span class="hljs-comment">// Given n, T, Q, bucket boundaries, and A with L-regions computed</span>
<span class="hljs-comment">// Note that these are freshly computed bucket boundaries, not those</span>
<span class="hljs-comment">// modified in the L phase. </span>
<span class="hljs-type">int</span> n;
vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> T, Q, head, tail, A;

<span class="hljs-keyword">auto</span> extend3 = [&](<span class="hljs-type">int</span> i) -> <span class="hljs-type">void</span>
{
    <span class="hljs-type">int</span> j = i - <span class="hljs-number">1</span>;
    <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span>(j >= <span class="hljs-number">0</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">and</span> <span class="hljs-built_in">is_S_type</span>(Q[j]))
    {
        tail[T[j]] --;
        A[tail[T[j]]] = j;
    }
};

<span class="hljs-comment">// place the sentinel position separately</span>
A[<span class="hljs-number">0</span>] = n;

<span class="hljs-comment">// induce S positions into A</span>
<span class="hljs-keyword">auto</span> s_induce = [&]() -> <span class="hljs-type">void</span>
{
    <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span>(<span class="hljs-type">int</span> i = n; i >= <span class="hljs-number">0</span>; i --)
        <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span>(A[i] != <span class="hljs-number">-1</span>)
            <span class="hljs-built_in">extend3</span>(A[i]);
};
<span class="hljs-built_in">s_induce</span>();
</code></pre>
</div>
</details>
<p>Why does this work? The proof is structurally symmetric to that of L-induce (we now process strings in non-increasing order, so we go from right to left in <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="A" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="A"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D434">𝐴</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="A"><mi data-latex="A">A</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>, and every call to <code>extend3(A[i])</code> can only add something to <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="A" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="A"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D434">𝐴</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="A"><mi data-latex="A">A</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> strictly before <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="i" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="i"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D456">𝑖</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="i"><mi data-latex="i">i</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>), but with one caveat: coverage previously relied on the fact that every sequence of L positions ended in an LMS position (every downward slope ends in a valley), and us manually placing the LMS positions into <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="A" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="A"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D434">𝐴</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="A"><mi data-latex="A">A</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> first. The equivalent requirement here would be every upward slope ending in a peak, and us having placed every peak first. As all L regions have already been computed, all the peaks have been placed into <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="A" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="A"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D434">𝐴</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="A"><mi data-latex="A">A</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>. The only source of nuisance is the very last position, which is LMS-type and doesn't have an L-type peak after it.</p>
<p>Thankfully:</p>
<ul>
<li><mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="T_n" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-msub data-latex="T_n"><mjx-mi data-latex="T"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D447">𝑇</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-script style="vertical-align: -0.15em; margin-left: -0.12em;"><mjx-mi size="s" data-latex="n"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D45B">𝑛</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-script></mjx-msub></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="T_n"><msub data-latex="T_n"><mi data-latex="T">T</mi><mi data-latex="n">n</mi></msub></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> is the unique minimum and must therefore be the very first element in <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="A" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="A"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D434">𝐴</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="A"><mi data-latex="A">A</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>, so we manually place it.</li>
<li>Because it's the unique minimum, <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="n - 1" breakable="true" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="n"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D45B">𝑛</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-break size="3"> </mjx-break><mjx-mo data-latex="-"><mjx-c class="mjx-c2212">−</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mn space="3" data-latex="1"><mjx-c class="mjx-c31">1</mjx-c></mjx-mn></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="n - 1"><mi data-latex="n">n</mi><mo data-latex="-">−</mo><mn data-latex="1">1</mn></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> is L-type. Therefore, all other S-type positions have some peak after them (a "Leftmost L type").</li>
</ul>
<p>I leave the formal proof of correctness to the reader, and return to the broader picture.</p>
<p>We now know that just having <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="G" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="G"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D43A">𝐺</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="G"><mi data-latex="G">G</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> would allow us to set off a convenient chain of events (the induction phases) which would end in <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="O(n)" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="O"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D442">𝑂</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mo data-latex="("><mjx-c class="mjx-c28">(</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mi data-latex="n"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D45B">𝑛</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mo data-latex=")"><mjx-c class="mjx-c29">)</mjx-c></mjx-mo></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="O(n)"><mi data-latex="O">O</mi><mo data-latex="(" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi data-latex="n">n</mi><mo data-latex=")" stretchy="false">)</mo></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> time, with us having computed <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="A" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="A"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D434">𝐴</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="A"><mi data-latex="A">A</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>. The entire problem therefore reduces to being able to sort the LMS-suffixes efficiently.</p>
<h1>5. Sorting LMS-suffixes</h1>
<p>Okay, so how do we sort LMS suffixes efficiently? The S induce would of course give us their sorted order, but that needs the L induce, which needs the sorted order... It's a bit of a chicken-and-egg problem.</p>
<p>Let's think outside the box. <p>Now, let's try to adapt our old procedure 2 to produce <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="C" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="C"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D436">𝐶</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="C"><mi data-latex="C">C</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>:</p>
<details><summary class="spoiler-summary">Procedure 5</summary>
<div class="spoiler-content">
<pre class="hljs"><code>C = [-1] * (n + 1)

put {T[i, i], i} for all LMS-type i into heap H, which uses the alex comparator

<span class="pseudo-comment"># just like our previous extend2 function, except here we insert T[j, E[j]] into the heap</span>
def extend2(i):
    j = i - 1
    if (j >= 0) and (position j is L-type)
        place j in the first empty position of the bucket of T[j] in C
        put {T[j, E[j]], j} into H

while H is not empty:
    pop out {v, i}, the smallest element of H
    extend2(i)
</code></pre>

<p>The observant reader will have noticed that our arguments have been almost identical to the initial use of L-induce. We shall continue in a similar vein. Consider this optimised version of procedure 5 (adapted from procedure 2.5):</p>
<details><summary class="spoiler-summary">Procedure 5.5</summary>
<div class="spoiler-content">
<pre class="hljs"><code>C = [-1] * (n + 1)

put {T[i, i], i} for all LMS-type i into heap H

<span class="pseudo-comment"># once again, we don't place anything into the heap any more</span>
def extend2(i):
    j = i - 1
    if (j >= 0) and (position j is L-type)
        place j in the first empty position of the bucket of T[j] in C

<span class="pseudo-comment"># we iterate over the first character of the suffix</span>
for character c from 0 to n:

    <span class="pseudo-comment"># we first process the L-region of c</span>
    let C[l, r] be the L-region for c
    for i from l to r:
        extend2(C[i])
  
    <span class="pseudo-comment"># we then process the LMS-types of c, naively</span>
    while H is not empty and the smallest string in H begins with c:
        pop out {T[i, i], i}, the smallest element of H
        extend2(i)
</code></pre>
</div>
</details>
<p>Why is this correct? The proof is almost identical to that of procedure 2.5 - <code>extend2(i)</code> is called over the same sequence of <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="i" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="i"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D456">𝑖</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="i"><mi data-latex="i">i</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>. The only subtlety is that while the strings in 2.5 were suffixes and could therefore not be equal to each other, strings here can be equal. Fortunately, the order in which equal strings are processed doesn't matter at all (so it's technically not the exact same sequence of <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="i" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="i"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D456">𝑖</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="i"><mi data-latex="i">i</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>, you can swap indices which correspond to the same string). All of this should be fairly natural by now, so I'll leave the formal proof to the reader.</p>
<p>Now, recall that at this point in the old L-induce, we revealed the need for <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="G" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="G"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D43A">𝐺</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="G"><mi data-latex="G">G</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>, as in procedure 2.5, we <em>needed</em> the heap to sort the LMS suffixes <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="T[E_i, n]" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="T"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D447">𝑇</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mo data-latex="["><mjx-c class="mjx-c5B">[</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-msub data-latex="E_i"><mjx-mi data-latex="E"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D438">𝐸</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-script style="vertical-align: -0.15em; margin-left: -0.028em;"><mjx-mi size="s" data-latex="i"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D456">𝑖</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-script></mjx-msub><mjx-mo data-latex=","><mjx-c class="mjx-c2C">,</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mi space="2" data-latex="n"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D45B">𝑛</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mo data-latex="]"><mjx-c class="mjx-c5D">]</mjx-c></mjx-mo></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="T[E_i, n]"><mi data-latex="T">T</mi><mo data-latex="[" stretchy="false">[</mo><msub data-latex="E_i"><mi data-latex="E">E</mi><mi data-latex="i">i</mi></msub><mo data-latex=",">,</mo><mi data-latex="n">n</mi><mo data-latex="]" stretchy="false">]</mo></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> for us. <pre class="hljs"><code><span class="hljs-comment">// Given n, T, Q, and the bucket boundaries (see code in theorem 2.4)</span>

<span class="hljs-function">vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> <span class="hljs-title">C</span><span class="hljs-params">(n + <span class="hljs-number">1</span>, <span class="hljs-number">-1</span>)</span></span>;

<span class="hljs-keyword">auto</span> extend2 = [&](<span class="hljs-type">int</span> i) -> <span class="hljs-type">void</span>
{

        head[T[j]] ++;
    }
};

{

        <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span>(C[i] != <span class="hljs-number">-1</span>)

<span class="hljs-built_in">l_induce</span>();

<p>The justification of its correctness is basically identical to that of procedure 3, and is left as an exercise to the reader.</p>
<p>Now that we have filled the L-regions of <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="C" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="C"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D436">𝐶</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="C"><mi data-latex="C">C</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>, we turn our attention back to the S-regions. <h1>6. Putting it all together</h1>
<p>Let's finally assemble our algorithm from the pieces we've painstakingly built:</p>
<pre class="hljs"><code><span class="pseudo-comment"># T satisfies conditions from section 1</span>
SA(T):
    N = |T|
    n = N - 1

    if N == 1:
        return [0]

    classify L, S, LMS types in O(n)

<span class="pseudo-comment">#PHASE 1: sort LMS substrings under alex</span>
    C = [-1] * (n + 1)
    seed C with T[i, i] for all LMS positions i, in O(n)
    run L induce on C   <span class="pseudo-comment"># we compute fresh bucket boundaries before every L and S induce</span>
    run S induce on C

<span class="pseudo-comment">#PHASE 2: construct T2 and sort its suffixes to get G</span>
    <span class="pseudo-comment">#label full LMS substrings</span>
    R = [-1] * (n + 1)
    label = -1, last = -1
    for i from 0 to n:
        if C[i] is LMS type:
            j = C[i]
            if last == -1 or !equal(last, j):     <span class="pseudo-comment">#equal(i, j) compares P[i] and P[j]</span>
                label += 1
            R[j] = label
            last = j
    <span class="pseudo-comment">#construct T2 and sort its suffixes</span>
    T2 = []
    for i from 0 to n:
        if i is LMS type:
            T2.append(R[i])
    A2 = SA(T2)
    <span class="pseudo-comment">#construct G from A2</span>
    G = A2
    for i from 0 to |G| - 1:
        G[i] = l[G[i]]  <span class="pseudo-comment">#l[i] is i-th LMS position in T</span>

<span class="pseudo-comment">#PHASE 3: seed A with G and run the final L and S induce </span>
    A = [-1] * (n + 1)
    seed A with G
    run L induce on A
    run S induce on A

    return A
</code></pre>
<p>My own <a href="https://github.com/welcome-to-the-sunny-side/libra/blob/main/string/suffix_array.cpp">implementation</a> of SAIS was unfortunately created before I wrote this blog, and doesn't really follow the exposition, but here's a highly readable one by my friend Opus 5.5 that does:</p>
<details><summary class="spoiler-summary">Code</summary>
<div class="spoiler-content">
<pre class="hljs"><code><span class="hljs-meta">#<span class="hljs-keyword">include</span> <span class="hljs-string"><bits/stdc++.h></span></span>
<span class="hljs-keyword">using</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">namespace</span> std;

<span class="hljs-comment">// Types of positions (section 2, 3). An LMS position is also S-type.</span>
<span class="hljs-keyword">enum</span> <span class="hljs-title class_">Type</span> : <span class="hljs-type">uint8_t</span> { L_TYPE, S_TYPE, LMS_TYPE };

<span class="hljs-comment">// Computes the suffix array of T.</span>
<span class="hljs-comment">// T must satisfy the conditions from section 1: with n = |T| - 1,</span>
<span class="hljs-comment">//   - T[n] == 0 is the sentinel (the unique minimum), and</span>
<span class="hljs-comment">//   - T[i] lies in [1, n] for all i < n.</span>
<span class="hljs-function">vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> <span class="hljs-title">SA</span><span class="hljs-params">(<span class="hljs-type">const</span> vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> &T)</span>
</span>{
    <span class="hljs-type">const</span> <span class="hljs-type">int</span> N = (<span class="hljs-type">int</span>)T.<span class="hljs-built_in">size</span>(), n = N - <span class="hljs-number">1</span>;

    <span class="hljs-comment">// base case</span>
    <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span>(N == <span class="hljs-number">1</span>)
        <span class="hljs-keyword">return</span> {<span class="hljs-number">0</span>};

    <span class="hljs-comment">// ---------------------------------------------------------------</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// Classify positions as L / S / LMS (theorem 2.3, section 3)</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// ---------------------------------------------------------------</span>
    <span class="hljs-function">vector<Type> <span class="hljs-title">Q</span><span class="hljs-params">(N)</span></span>;
    Q[n] = S_TYPE;
    <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span>(<span class="hljs-type">int</span> i = n - <span class="hljs-number">1</span>; i >= <span class="hljs-number">0</span>; i --)
    {
        <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span>(T[i] < T[i + <span class="hljs-number">1</span>])
            Q[i] = S_TYPE;
        <span class="hljs-keyword">else</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span>(T[i] > T[i + <span class="hljs-number">1</span>])
            Q[i] = L_TYPE;
        <span class="hljs-keyword">else</span>
            Q[i] = Q[i + <span class="hljs-number">1</span>];
    }

    vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> l;      <span class="hljs-comment">// l[k] = k-th LMS position, so l = {l_0 < l_1 < ... < l_{m - 1}}</span>
    <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span>(<span class="hljs-type">int</span> i = <span class="hljs-number">1</span>; i <= n; i ++)
        <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span>(Q[i] == S_TYPE <span class="hljs-keyword">and</span> Q[i - <span class="hljs-number">1</span>] == L_TYPE)
        {
            Q[i] = LMS_TYPE;
            l.<span class="hljs-built_in">push_back</span>(i);
        }
    <span class="hljs-type">const</span> <span class="hljs-type">int</span> m = (<span class="hljs-type">int</span>)l.<span class="hljs-built_in">size</span>();

    <span class="hljs-keyword">auto</span> is_L = [&](<span class="hljs-type">int</span> i) { <span class="hljs-keyword">return</span> Q[i] == L_TYPE; };
    <span class="hljs-keyword">auto</span> is_S = [&](<span class="hljs-type">int</span> i) { <span class="hljs-keyword">return</span> Q[i] != L_TYPE; };
    <span class="hljs-keyword">auto</span> is_LMS = [&](<span class="hljs-type">int</span> i) { <span class="hljs-keyword">return</span> Q[i] == LMS_TYPE; };

    <span class="hljs-comment">// ---------------------------------------------------------------</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// Bucket boundaries (section 2): the bucket for symbol c is [head[c], tail[c])</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// ---------------------------------------------------------------</span>
    <span class="hljs-function">vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> <span class="hljs-title">cnt</span><span class="hljs-params">(N, <span class="hljs-number">0</span>)</span></span>;      <span class="hljs-comment">// symbols lie in [0, n]</span>
    <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span>(<span class="hljs-type">int</span> x : T)
        cnt[x] ++;

    <span class="hljs-comment">// induce L/S both modify the boundaries, so we hand out fresh copies every time</span>
    <span class="hljs-keyword">auto</span> get_buckets = [&](vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> &head, vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> &tail) -> <span class="hljs-type">void</span>
    {
        head.<span class="hljs-built_in">assign</span>(N, <span class="hljs-number">0</span>);
        tail.<span class="hljs-built_in">assign</span>(N, <span class="hljs-number">0</span>);
        <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span>(<span class="hljs-type">int</span> c = <span class="hljs-number">0</span>, sum = <span class="hljs-number">0</span>; c < N; c ++)
        {
            head[c] = sum;
            sum += cnt[c];
            tail[c] = sum;
        }
    };

    <span class="hljs-comment">// ---------------------------------------------------------------</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// Induced sorting (section 4)</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">//</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// `seeds` contains the LMS positions, in sorted order. Returns the array</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// obtained by seeding them at the tails of their S-buckets, then running</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// L-induce (procedure 3) followed by S-induce (procedure 4).</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">//</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// Phase 1 and phase 3 differ *only* in the seeds they pass here.</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// ---------------------------------------------------------------</span>
    <span class="hljs-keyword">auto</span> induced_sort = [&](<span class="hljs-type">const</span> vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> &seeds) -> vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>>
    {
        vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> <span class="hljs-built_in">A</span>(N, <span class="hljs-number">-1</span>);
        vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> head, tail;

        <span class="hljs-comment">// seeding: walk the seeds from largest to smallest, filling each S-bucket from its tail</span>
        <span class="hljs-built_in">get_buckets</span>(head, tail);
        <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span>(<span class="hljs-type">int</span> k = (<span class="hljs-type">int</span>)seeds.<span class="hljs-built_in">size</span>() - <span class="hljs-number">1</span>; k >= <span class="hljs-number">0</span>; k --)
        {
            <span class="hljs-type">int</span> i = seeds[k];
            A[-- tail[T[i]]] = i;
        }

        <span class="hljs-comment">// L-induce: walk left to right; if A[i] - 1 is L-type, append it to the</span>
        <span class="hljs-comment">// first free slot of its L-bucket (this is extend2)</span>
        <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span>(<span class="hljs-type">int</span> i = <span class="hljs-number">0</span>; i < N; i ++)
        {
            <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span>(A[i] == <span class="hljs-number">-1</span>)
                <span class="hljs-keyword">continue</span>;
            <span class="hljs-type">int</span> j = A[i] - <span class="hljs-number">1</span>;
            <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span>(j >= <span class="hljs-number">0</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">and</span> <span class="hljs-built_in">is_L</span>(j))
                A[head[T[j]] ++] = j;
        }

        <span class="hljs-comment">// clean up: remove the seeded LMS positions, the S-induce places them again</span>
        <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span>(<span class="hljs-type">int</span> i = <span class="hljs-number">0</span>; i < N; i ++)
            <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span>(A[i] != <span class="hljs-number">-1</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">and</span> <span class="hljs-built_in">is_LMS</span>(A[i]))
                A[i] = <span class="hljs-number">-1</span>;

        <span class="hljs-comment">// S-induce: walk right to left; if A[i] - 1 is S-type, prepend it to the</span>
        <span class="hljs-comment">// last free slot of its S-bucket (this is extend3)</span>
        <span class="hljs-built_in">get_buckets</span>(head, tail);
        A[<span class="hljs-number">0</span>] = n;               <span class="hljs-comment">// the sentinel is the smallest suffix, place it manually</span>
        <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span>(<span class="hljs-type">int</span> i = n; i >= <span class="hljs-number">0</span>; i --)
        {
            <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span>(A[i] == <span class="hljs-number">-1</span>)
                <span class="hljs-keyword">continue</span>;
            <span class="hljs-type">int</span> j = A[i] - <span class="hljs-number">1</span>;
            <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span>(j >= <span class="hljs-number">0</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">and</span> <span class="hljs-built_in">is_S</span>(j))
                A[-- tail[T[j]]] = j;
        }

        <span class="hljs-keyword">return</span> A;
    };

    <span class="hljs-comment">// ---------------------------------------------------------------</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// PHASE 1: sort all LMS substrings under alex (section 5.2)</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">//</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// Seeding with T[i, i] for each LMS position i: these are single</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// characters, so any order works, as long as each one lands in its own</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// bucket (procedure 6).</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// ---------------------------------------------------------------</span>
    vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> C = <span class="hljs-built_in">induced_sort</span>(l);

    <span class="hljs-comment">// ---------------------------------------------------------------</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// PHASE 2: label full LMS substrings, build T2, recurse (sections 5.1, 6)</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// ---------------------------------------------------------------</span>

    <span class="hljs-comment">// equal(i, j) checks whether P_i == P_j for LMS positions i != j.</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// P_i = T[i, E_i] ends at the next LMS position, so we walk both substrings</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// together until one of them ends. They are equal iff both end at the same</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// offset with all characters equal along the way.</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// (If one of them is the sentinel n, the very first characters differ, so</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// we never read past the end of T.)</span>
    <span class="hljs-keyword">auto</span> equal = [&](<span class="hljs-type">int</span> i, <span class="hljs-type">int</span> j) -> <span class="hljs-type">bool</span>
    {
        <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span>(<span class="hljs-type">int</span> k = <span class="hljs-number">0</span>; ; k ++)
        {
            <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span>(T[i + k] != T[j + k])
                <span class="hljs-keyword">return</span> <span class="hljs-literal">false</span>;
            <span class="hljs-type">bool</span> end_i = (k > <span class="hljs-number">0</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">and</span> <span class="hljs-built_in">is_LMS</span>(i + k));
            <span class="hljs-type">bool</span> end_j = (k > <span class="hljs-number">0</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">and</span> <span class="hljs-built_in">is_LMS</span>(j + k));
            <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span>(end_i <span class="hljs-keyword">or</span> end_j)
                <span class="hljs-keyword">return</span> end_i <span class="hljs-keyword">and</span> end_j;
        }
    };

    <span class="hljs-comment">// walk C (which is alex-sorted) and give equal full LMS substrings equal labels</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// R[i] = label of P_i, for LMS positions i</span>
    <span class="hljs-function">vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> <span class="hljs-title">R</span><span class="hljs-params">(N, <span class="hljs-number">-1</span>)</span></span>;
    <span class="hljs-type">int</span> label = <span class="hljs-number">-1</span>, last = <span class="hljs-number">-1</span>;
    <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span>(<span class="hljs-type">int</span> k = <span class="hljs-number">0</span>; k < N; k ++)
    {
        <span class="hljs-type">int</span> j = C[k];
        <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span>(!<span class="hljs-built_in">is_LMS</span>(j))
            <span class="hljs-keyword">continue</span>;
        <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span>(last == <span class="hljs-number">-1</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">or</span> !<span class="hljs-built_in">equal</span>(last, j))
            label ++;
        R[j] = label;
        last = j;
    }
    <span class="hljs-comment">// C[0] = n is the first LMS position seen, so the sentinel gets label 0,</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// and every other label lies in [1, m - 1]: T2 satisfies section 1</span>

    <span class="hljs-comment">// T2[k] = label of the k-th full LMS substring</span>
    <span class="hljs-function">vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> <span class="hljs-title">T2</span><span class="hljs-params">(m)</span></span>;
    <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span>(<span class="hljs-type">int</span> k = <span class="hljs-number">0</span>; k < m; k ++)
        T2[k] = R[l[k]];

    <span class="hljs-comment">// G = LMS positions in sorted order of their suffixes</span>
    vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> G = <span class="hljs-built_in">SA</span>(T2);
    <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span>(<span class="hljs-type">int</span> k = <span class="hljs-number">0</span>; k < m; k ++)
        G[k] = l[G[k]];

    <span class="hljs-comment">// ---------------------------------------------------------------</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// PHASE 3: seed with G and induce the actual suffix array (section 4)</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment">// ---------------------------------------------------------------</span>
    <span class="hljs-keyword">return</span> <span class="hljs-built_in">induced_sort</span>(G);
}

<span class="hljs-comment">// Convenience wrapper for arbitrary non-negative input: s[i] in [0, K).</span>
<span class="hljs-comment">// Remaps s to satisfy section 1 in O(n + K), and drops the sentinel from the result.</span>
<span class="hljs-function">vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> <span class="hljs-title">suffix_array</span><span class="hljs-params">(<span class="hljs-type">const</span> vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> &s, <span class="hljs-type">int</span> K)</span>
</span>{
    <span class="hljs-type">const</span> <span class="hljs-type">int</span> n = (<span class="hljs-type">int</span>)s.<span class="hljs-built_in">size</span>();

    <span class="hljs-comment">// rank[x] = 1 + number of distinct symbols in s smaller than x</span>
    <span class="hljs-function">vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> <span class="hljs-title">rank</span><span class="hljs-params">(K, <span class="hljs-number">0</span>)</span></span>;
    <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span>(<span class="hljs-type">int</span> x : s)
        rank[x] = <span class="hljs-number">1</span>;
    <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span>(<span class="hljs-type">int</span> x = <span class="hljs-number">0</span>, r = <span class="hljs-number">0</span>; x < K; x ++)
        <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span>(rank[x])
            rank[x] = ++ r;

    <span class="hljs-function">vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> <span class="hljs-title">T</span><span class="hljs-params">(n + <span class="hljs-number">1</span>)</span></span>;
    <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span>(<span class="hljs-type">int</span> i = <span class="hljs-number">0</span>; i < n; i ++)
        T[i] = rank[s[i]];
    T[n] = <span class="hljs-number">0</span>;

    vector<<span class="hljs-type">int</span>> A = <span class="hljs-built_in">SA</span>(T);
    <span class="hljs-keyword">return</span> <span class="hljs-built_in">vector</span><<span class="hljs-type">int</span>>(A.<span class="hljs-built_in">begin</span>() + <span class="hljs-number">1</span>, A.<span class="hljs-built_in">end</span>());     <span class="hljs-comment">// A[0] is always the sentinel</span>
}
</code></pre>
</div>
